pass_a_gloss: Rescue from sword the soul of-me. And toward the holy God-bearer the Simeon says: And of-you and herself the soul will-pass-through a-sword. And out-of hand of-dog the only-begotten of-me. In-singular and now, whom he-said above dogs, through the race he-calls. Only-begotten and the own soul he-said, as alone sin not having-known; but also that alone through all she-had of-the God Word the union. Perhaps and the having-stood-beside church to-him he-says only-begotten, not having spot or wrinkle, out-of the blameless perfectly having-been-filled-up, of-which according-to progress into various ranks having-been-divided; sixty indeed are queens, eighty and concubines, and young-women of-whom not is number; above and all is dove perfect, only-begotten being to-the mother the above Jerusalem.
pass_b_english: “Rescue my soul from the sword” (Psalm 21:21). And to the holy God-bearer Simeon says: “And a sword will pass through your own soul also” (Luke 2:35). “And my only-begotten from the hand of the dog.”

And now in the singular he names, by the race, those whom he called dogs above. And he called his own soul only-begotten, as alone not having known sin; but also because it alone through all had the union of the God-Word.

And perhaps he calls the church that stood beside him only-begotten, not having spot or wrinkle, perfectly completed from the blameless, which according to progress is divided into various ranks: “sixty are queens, and eighty concubines, and maidens of whom there is no number; but above all is a perfect dove, being only-begotten to the mother, the Jerusalem above” (Song of Songs 6:8-9).

choices.term: Μονογενῆ δὲ τὴν ἰδίαν ψυχὴν εἶπεν, ὡς μόνην ἁμαρτίαν μὴ γνοῦσαν
choices.english: he called his own soul only-begotten, as alone not having known sin
choices.why: μονογενῆ is the soul without sin, not a second Son. OCR γνοῦ σαν.
rejected: the only-begotten is a second Son beside the Word

choices.term: τὴν παραστᾶσαν ἐκκλησίαν αὐτῷ λέγει μονογενῆ, μὴ ἔχουσαν σπῖλον ἢ ῥυτίδα
choices.english: he calls the church that stood beside him only-begotten, not having spot or wrinkle
choices.why: Second reading: church as only-begotten. Not ‘the church is the Theotokos’ as the whole gloss.
rejected: the church has spot and wrinkle
